rendered:
The text does not give exact numbers for these. The values below are estimates read off the bar chart in panel (h) of Fig. 1[1] (the chart's labels are spelled "L-HNGRs" and "BA@L-HNGRs"):
- BA: about −7 mV[2], the only negative value, with an error bar spanning roughly −5.5 to −8.5 mV[3].
- L-HGNRs: about +7 mV[4].
- BA@L-HGNRs: about +4 mV[5], which is lower than for the L-HGNRs alone.
The authors say this change in zeta potential, along with other evidence, supports the idea that BA was attached to the HGNR surface.[6]

source.label: Fig. 1
source.caption: Fig. 1. Characterization of HGNRs and BA@L-HGNRs. (a) Transmission electron microscopy imaging of L-HGNRs; (b) EDS elemental (Au, Ag, S) mapping images of L-HGNRs; (c) CD of L/D-HGNRs; (d) g-factor spectra of L/D-HGNRs; (e) XPS spectra of BA@L-HGNRs; (f) CD of L-HGNRs and BA@L-HGNRs; (g) UV–vis spectra of L- HGNRs and BA@L-HGNRs; (h) zeta potential measurements of BA, L-HGNRs and BA@L-HGNRs.

source.text: In panel h, BA has a zeta potential of about −7 mV, with an error bar spanning roughly −5.5 to −8.5 mV.
